title: This banking giant is setting up for a breakout. What levels to watch
raw_text: While many more companies report earnings over the next two weeks, a large portion of the financial sector has already released results. That helps reduce some of the company-specific risk within the group and could potentially lead to less volatility among XLF components in aggregate. The XLF Financials ETF itself has spent the last several weeks consolidating after its sharp rebound from the late-March low. Thus far, that digestion phase has been relatively orderly and has taken place while remaining above its key 50-day moving average. Thus, if here is any short-term rotation out of technology after its historic rally, financials could become a logical area for investors to revisit. The sector has lagged the aggressive momentum seen in the likes of semiconductors recently, but that also means many financial stocks are not nearly as extended from a technical perspective. If there is going to be renewed participation within financials, the largest components inside XLF will likely need to lead the move. One of those, of course, is Goldman Sachs . Long-time CappThesis clients know we have profiled GS multiple times over the last year because it has consistently done a very good job leveraging bullish pattern breakouts. Similar to XLF, GS has reclaimed its 50-day moving average during the recent comeback effort. More importantly, the stock currently sits further above its own 50-day moving average than XLF does relative to its own 50-day line, which highlights its improving relative strength within the sector (more on this below). With the rebound from the March lows combined with the price action dating back to February, GS now appears to be tracing out a potential inverse head-and-shoulders pattern. The stock has steadily worked through a series of higher lows while momentum has improved along the way. A breakout through the area just below 950 would complete the formation and imply an upside target near 1,110 based on the measured move of the pattern. For risk management purposes, we are using a stop just below the right shoulder near 888. Beyond the absolute chart setup, GS has also formed a bullish relative pattern versus XLF itself. Both the absolute and relative formations have been developing since the beginning of 2026. Needless to say, if GS can eventually break out on both an absolute and relative basis versus the second-largest sector in the SPX, then the setup would continue to support the potential for additional upside and, ultimately, a move toward new all-time highs. The final chart removes GS' actual price action and instead focuses strictly on the 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages, shown in green, blue, and red, respectively. Specifically, we are highlighting the four instances, including the current one, when the 20-day moving average crossed above the 50-day while both were starting to slope higher and positioned above the 200-day moving average, as well. In each prior occurrence, the stock went on to experience additional upside over the ensuing months. That setup becomes particularly constructive when the 200-day moving average is also trending higher, which was true in those prior examples and has now occurred once again. Given the strengthening momentum backdrop and the potential inverse head-and-shoulders breakout, another constructive intermediate-term setup may be developing for GS. — Frank Cappelleri Founder: https://cappthesis.com DISCLOSURES: None.
